versions.content: Resolving Variation Points along the Development Steps Every variation point starts in the XML representation, but is not necessarily resolved in the XML representation. If it is not resolved in a particular processing step, it needs to be transferred to the output artifacts. For example, this means that generated C headers may contain #ifdef statements (for PreCompile Time variability). Another example is PostBuild variation, where the generated object code contains con- ditional statements for implementing the PostBuild variation points, as specified in the XML representation.
